title: Rabbi Dostai son of Rabbi Yehudah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: (A Tanna of a baraita in Rabbi’s generation.) Hyman finds him always mentioned by this name, except in Bava Kamma 83b as Ben Yehudah. He was a student of Rabbi Shimon, as in Chullin 123a, where he spoke in his name; in Arakhin 30a he disagrees with Rabbi; and in Tosefta Sheviit 2:14, a dispute with Rabbi Yose ben Kifar. His halakhot we find in Kiddushin 64a, where he said, “The daughters of Israel are a ritual bath of purification for disqualified Kohanim (chalalim)”; Bava Kamma 83b, “An eye for an eye — money”; Tosefta Makkot 1:6, “Plotting witnesses whom others came and discredited: those who discredited them are exempt”; and Tosefta Sanhedrin, end of chapter 3, “Rabbi Dostai son of Rabbi Yehudah says: If he fled from the Land to abroad, his judgment is not reopened.” The statement is cited in Berakhot 7b, and there “Rabbi Yehudah ben Dostai in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Shetach”; but in Dikdukei Soferim Hyman regards the straightforward reading as “Rabbi Dostai son of Rabbi Yehudah in the name of Rabbi Shimon.” In Derekh Eretz, chapter 2, an aggadic saying of his remains, where he said: “Always provoke the wicked,” etc. Hyman suggests that it is likely that he was the son of Rabbi Yehudah, according to the chronology.

notes.text: חללין means disqualified Kohanim, not all disqualified people. Saved Machon Mamre Tosefta Makkot1:6 has זוממיהן פטורים: those who discredited the plotting witnesses are exempt, not necessarily the original witnesses. The English-version request returned no versions and is preserved. שטו/בקד״ס/בד״אד are read contextually as שטח/בדק״ס/Derekh Eretz, and Hyman’s son-of-Yehudah inference stays tentative.

The inspected Machon Mamre Tosefta Makkot 1:6 reads זוממיהן פטורים, with the exempt subject being those who discredited the plotting witnesses. It is not an independent inspection of another Tosefta edition. Hyman’s always wording, preferred name chains, contextual abbreviation readings and tentative son-of-Yehudah chronology are preserved, not converted into new identity relations.
